text: Have you ever wondered why you feel super energetic after eating a bowl of rice, but a bit sleepy after a heavy meal of sweets? Or why athletes eat lots of bananas during a match? Food is not just stuff that fills our stomach; it’s a magical fuel that our body uses to perform miracles every day.
Imagine your body is an advanced sports car. What would happen if you put water in the fuel tank instead of petrol? Why can't we just survive on water and air?

Just like a car needs the right fuel to run, oil to keep the engine smooth, and metal to build its body, our body needs different types of 'materials' from food. These materials do different jobs: some give energy, some repair broken parts, and some protect us from getting sick.

content.title: The Body as a Machine
content.description: Visualizing how food acts as fuel, building blocks, and protective shields.

text: These essential materials are called Nutrients. There are five major components of food: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Vitamins, and Minerals. Water and roughage (dietary fibers) are also crucial but they don't provide nutrients themselves.

content.definition: Chemical substances present in food that our body needs to grow, survive, and fight diseases. Derived from Latin 'nutrire' (to nourish). In Hindi: Poshak Tatva (Nutrients).

question: If your body is like a machine, what role do Nutrients play?
options: They only make the food taste good.
They provide materials for energy, growth, and repair.
They only help us sleep better.

text: Take a moment. Explain to yourself (or a friend) what would happen if you only ate one type of food, like just chocolate, every single day?

Think about how this connects to what you learned in Chapter 1 about 'Where does food come from?'. Plants give us different nutrients than animals. A cow eats grass, which has nutrients, and when we drink the cow's milk, we get protein and calcium!

content.title: The Plate Challenge
content.description: Look at what you had for lunch today. Can you identify which item gave you energy (carbohydrates) and which one helped in your growth (proteins)?

text: Have you ever felt completely exhausted after running a short race, while some kids keep playing for hours without getting tired? What's their secret? Let's look closer at Carbohydrates.
Why do we eat sweet things or bread when we need quick energy? What is inside them that wakes us up?

Think of a campfire. To keep the fire burning bright and hot, you need dry wood. Carbohydrates are the 'dry wood' for the fire inside your cells. When you eat them, your body quickly burns them to create energy.

content.title: Carbohydrates as Fuel
content.description: Showing molecules of carbohydrates breaking down into energy bursts.

text: Carbohydrates are our main source of energy. They come in two forms: sugars (quick energy, like in fruits) and starch (long-lasting energy, like in potatoes, rice, and wheat).

content.definition: Energy-giving nutrients primarily found in plants. The word comes from 'carbo' (carbon) and 'hydrate' (water). In Hindi: Karbohaidret (Carbohydrates).

question: Which of the following foods would give you the quickest burst of energy before a race?

content.text: Vedic Connection: Ancient Indian texts like Ayurveda emphasize eating grains like rice and wheat (which are rich in carbohydrates) during the day when our 'digestive fire' (Jatharagni) is highest.
Many students think Fats and Carbohydrates are the same because they both give energy. Remember: Carbohydrates give QUICK energy, while Fats store energy for LATER use (like a battery).

text: If you fall down and scratch your knee, how does new skin magically appear after a few days? What builds that new skin?
If Carbohydrates are the fuel for the car, what repairs the broken engine parts?
Imagine a wall made of Lego bricks. Every day, some bricks get old and break. You need new bricks to replace them and to make the wall taller. Proteins are the Lego bricks of your body.

content.title: Proteins as Building Blocks
content.description: Visualizing protein molecules snapping together like Lego bricks to heal a wound.

text: Proteins are body-building foods. They help in the growth of our body and in repairing damaged cells. Foods like milk, eggs, pulses (dal), and meat are rich in proteins.

content.definition: Body-building nutrients essential for growth and repair of body cells. Derived from the Greek word 'proteios' meaning 'primary' or 'holding the first place'. In Hindi: Protin (Proteins).

question: If you want to grow taller and build strong muscles, which food should you include more in your diet?

text: Teach someone else: Why do growing children need more protein than adults? Explain it using the Lego bricks analogy.
Proteins also connect to the immune system. The antibodies that fight off viruses in your blood are actually made of proteins!

content.title: Protein Detective
content.description: Next time you are at the grocery store, check the nutrition labels on 3 different snacks. Which one has the highest protein content per 100g?
